newsitem.title: UK: BBC picks TCI as subscription TV partner.
newsitem.headline: BBC picks TCI as subscription TV partner.

text.p: The British Broadcasting Corporation said on Friday that its board had agreed to enter into exclusive negotiations with Flextech Plc and Discovery Communications Inc to create a series of subscription television channels.
Cable and satellite programming company Flextech, which is controlled by America's biggest cable TV operator, Tele-Communications Inc (TCI), will develop channels for the British market.
Discovery Communications, of which TCI is also a major shareholder, will develop channels for international markets.
BBC said the intention was for BBC Worldwide Ltd, its commercial arm, to conclude final agreements on the creation of separate joint ventures before the end of the year.
It said the target date for the launch of the Flextech/BBC channels was summer 1997.
BBC and Flextech are already partners in UK Gold, a subscription channel showing vintage shows.
British media group Pearson Plc and Cox Communications of the U.S. are also partners in UK Gold.
Cox, along with TCI and Advance/Newhouse, are major shareholders in Discovery Communications.
Satellite broadcaster BSkyB, in which Rupert Murdoch's News Corp is the largest shareholder, had been competing with Flextech to link up with the BBC in the field of subscription TV.
Although BSkyB has lost out, the BBC still wants to harness its extensive pay TV distribution network.

"An important part of the task before us will be to continue discussions with BSkyB and other distributors so that together we can establish a compelling proposition for the digital age," Bob Phillis, BBC Worldwide's chief executive, said in a statement.
The BBC has been under pressure to beef up its commercial activities after politicians criticised its demand for an increase in the licence fee above the rate of inflation.
TV owners pay a licence fee of 89.50 stg a year to fund the BBC. An above-inflation rise in the fee would be the first since 1985.

The public service broadcaster's huge library and production facilties makes it an idea partner for cable and satellite broadcasters seeking to compile attractive programme packages. Richard Emery, BBC Worldwide television's managing director, said BBC Worldwide would both sell programmes to the new channels to be created by the joint ventures and share in their ownership.
"We believe this will greatly increase our ability not only to continue to augment the licence fee, but also to maximise in future the commercial value of BBC programmes," Emery said.
